questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It makes cross traffic easier to see.
It stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As your speed increases, you must watch more carefully for hazards.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Your tires work less well when you drive faster.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
The road gets more slippery when you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires work less well when you drive faster.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water from the road as well. If you drive too fast, your tires may lose grip and you will hydroplane, sliding on a layer of water.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When you enter a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights in fog. High beams bounce off fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly all the time.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at a constant speed.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A good defensive driver watches other drivers and anticipates problems they might cause, even though other drivers may become distracted.

questions.question: How can you avoid a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Don't drive beside them and don't follow too closely.
Flash your lights at them.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't drive beside them and don't follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and rear. Avoid driving next to them and do not tailgate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Wildlife crossing.
School crossing or school zone.
Pedestrian crossing.
Business district.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing or school zone.
questions.explanation: Five-sided signs warn you that a school is nearby. Watch for children and pedestrians. This sign means there is a school crossing or school zone ahead.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so badly they look drunk.
Opening a window and turning up the radio will keep them alert.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so badly they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly they appear to be drunk. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to make them safe drivers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means you cannot do that action. This sign shows you cannot turn right.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop right away and block their path.
Do everything you can to clear their path.
Signal when it is safe for them to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear their path.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, clear a path for them. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road to let them pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: A flagger is a person controlling traffic in a construction area. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead.

questions.question: To be ready for hazards ahead, you should:

options.text: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Maintain focus toward the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
questions.explanation: You must look far ahead and scan the entire road, including the sides. This helps you spot problems before they become dangerous. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: If you are in an accident that oncoming traffic cannot see, you should:

options.text: Have someone warn approaching traffic.
Let oncoming traffic watch out for themselves.
Let the police handle everything.
Assume other drivers will have heard the crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have someone warn approaching traffic.
questions.explanation: Warn oncoming drivers to prevent more crashes. Have someone signal approaching cars. Keep a flashlight and flares in your vehicle for emergencies.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, you should expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Children may not understand traffic danger. Slow down and be extra careful in areas where children are present because they may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: Distracted drivers have a higher crash risk when using which of these?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players all distract you from driving. Even hands-free phones are dangerous. Any audio device can increase your crash risk.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or air horns and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so proceed only when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Look for turning vehicles before crossing a street.
Never run alongside or across a street.
Walk on the left side of the street, facing traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not run alongside or across streets. Walk on the left side facing oncoming traffic. Always look for turning vehicles before crossing.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means stop before the intersection. You must also stop at any stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to indicate they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right if you arrive at the same time. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver going much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic flow is hazardous. On two-lane roads, you must pull over and let traffic pass if you are slowing down other drivers. Only drive significantly below the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers and pedestrians when they may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down to listen for an approaching train.
Continue only when a flagger tells you it is safe.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow all their instructions.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Proceed normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, give them the right-of-way, and proceed with caution. Be ready to stop to prevent injury.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When conditions are not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when any condition is not perfect. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on a layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase the risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires help improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the most difficult driving season. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children walking on the side of the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: When a police officer asks you to take a blood alcohol test, you:

options.text: Do not have to take it if you can prove you weren't drinking.
Must take it or risk losing your license.
Do not have to take it if you haven't violated a traffic rule.
Must take it or risk a fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must take it or risk losing your license.
questions.explanation: When you operate a vehicle, you agree to be tested for blood alcohol content when requested by police. Refusing the test will result in loss of your license for at least one year.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same as a circular red light.
It means drivers may turn in the direction shown.
It means traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a circular red light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow has the same meaning as a circular red light. When the arrow is red, traffic in that lane must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
